verdict.rationale: Daytona's docs say each sandbox gets a dedicated kernel, filesystem, network stack and allocated vCPU/RAM/disk, which describes VM-level isolation. They also offer explicit VM sandboxes (a dedicated Linux VM or Windows VM), and a per-sandbox egress firewall adds to the boundary. Missing for 10: the docs never name the isolation technology (microVM, hypervisor), the separate 'container sandboxes' mode leaves it unclear whether every sandbox type has a hard boundary, and there is no independent or hands-on confirmation of the isolation guarantees.
